entries.label: Version 1
entries.prompt:
You are designing a new front end for this repository: a Python multi-agent
deep-research engine whose interface is FastAPI. The target is a React/Next front
end on that API, for a single local user, with no authentication.
Ground yourself first: read README.md, src/deep_research/api/app.py, and the SSE
event definitions that module streams.
The API serves today:
- POST /research -> session_id, status, current_agent, iteration, started_at,
  finished_at, report_path, trace_url, errors
- GET /research/{id}/status -> the same session shape
- GET /research/{id}/stream -> server-sent progress events, replayed from the
  first event and then followed live until the session reaches a terminal state
- GET /research/{id}/report -> the report as Markdown, only once complete
- GET /research/{id}/trace -> the LangSmith trace URL, absent while running
Product facts the design system cannot know:
- a run lasts minutes to tens of minutes and is watched, not clicked
- the report is the deliverable; progress and observability are supporting evidence
- a run can end partially, with iterations exhausted and errors recorded -- a
  normal outcome, not a crash
- local and single-user: no collaborators, orgs, billing or sharing surfaces
Define the status mapping explicitly in docs/design/DESIGN.md, using the active
design system's existing roles: running, completed, partially completed, failed,
and unavailable. Unavailable means a trace URL, token count or usage figure that
is simply absent -- it renders as muted text, never as a zero, a placeholder, or
a disabled control.
Task -- design artifacts only. Write no application code and run no npm install.
1. Propose three structurally distinct layouts for the investigation state, for
   example a linear event timeline, a narrative column with a details rail, or a
   split ledger of claims against sources. All three must use the active design
   system's tokens. For each: what it optimises, what it costs, and who it suits.
   Recommend one.
2. docs/design/DESIGN.md: the screen inventory, the status mapping above, and only
   the decisions the active design system does not already answer.
3. Build a self-contained prototype at docs/design/prototype/index.html with an
   in-page state switcher covering new research, running with live progress,
   completed report, and session history; plus docs/design/prototype/states.html
   covering empty, configuration error, session failed, and partial report. No
   build step, no external scripts, no web-font fetches, all values driven from
   the design system tokens through CSS custom properties, any details rail
   stacks below the primary column on narrow screens, visible focus states, and
   respect for prefers-reduced-motion.
4. List, per screen, the data it needs that the API above does not serve.
Keep every artifact under docs/design/. Do not modify src/, tests/ or
configuration, and do not commit anything -- leave the changes in the working
tree for review.
When you are done, tell me what to look at first and what you would change with
more time.@Perplexity AI

entries.label: Version 2
entries.prompt:
I want to redesign this. 

1. I want one page where there is a side bar which can be toggled and can see the history of the old reports and can go to them or look into the details of them.
2. I want the new research page to take in the text input from me. Max iteration, output format are not needed anymore. Model and reasoning effort, should be selected with a plus sign in the chat box itself. Output directory can stay as an option
3. Once it is submitted, it should automatically switch to something like the running page and it does not need to show all the events and the tail. It need to show the pipeline, session facts and cost and usage. 
4. Once it goes through the entire process, it should show the completed report in the same page

Make this redesign so that all of them are in the same page and get automatically changed with a transition. Separate session state tabs are not necessary and they should change dynamically based on the current state
